beats.label: S1 · Twins born sighted
beats.text: Twins who can see are born to Maghra. Baba's tribe fight off the Witchfinders and flee across a hidden bridge, which he collapses behind them to buy a new home.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the premise the whole series turns on: sighted children the Payan crown wants dead.

beats.label: S1 · The books, twelve summers on
beats.text: For twelve years the twins are hidden. Paris finally hands Kofun and Haniwa the box of books Jerlamarel left, telling them their real father can see.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The twins' knowledge and hunger to find Jerlamarel drives every road they take from here.

beats.label: S1 · Hunted downriver, Kanzua drowned
beats.text: Gether Bax betrays the tribe's new location; the Witchfinders sack it, and Baba's family flee downriver as Queen Kane collapses the Kanzua dam to drown her own rebels.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the Kanzua lie Kane will later blame on Trivantes to justify war.

beats.label: S1 · Maghra is royalty
beats.text: Cornered by the Witchfinders, Maghra reveals her father's royal rattle-ring. Tamacti Jun bows to her — she is Princess Maghra of House Kane, Queen Kane's younger sister.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The reveal that reroutes the whole show: the fugitive mother is a rival heir to the throne hunting her.

beats.label: S1 · Sisters take the crown together
beats.text: Tamacti Jun and Maghra rescue Queen Kane from slavery in the City of Worms. The sisters take joint command of the Witchfinder army and turn it toward Maghra's family.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Maghra inside the palace her family is running from — the whole S2 political trap.

beats.label: S1 · Jerlamarel's betrayal
beats.text: At the House of Enlightenment, Jerlamarel prepares to trade Haniwa to Trivantian General Edo Voss — Baba's estranged brother. Baba blinds him and flees with Kofun.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Edo and the Baba/Edo brother-feud that anchors S2.

beats.label: S1 · Tamacti down, Haniwa taken
beats.text: Queen Kane and Boots murder Tamacti Jun; the sisters address the Witchfinder army as joint rulers. Haniwa is delivered to Edo in Trivantes as Baba closes on the city.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The exact configuration S2 opens on: family split across two hostile capitals.

cliffhanger.text: Haniwa is a Trivantian prisoner of Baba's own brother. Maghra sits on a throne beside the sister who tried to kill her children, dispatching the Witchfinder army to find her family, while Baba and Kofun approach Edo's capital blind.
questions: Can Baba reach Haniwa inside his own brother's stronghold?
What will Maghra do when she learns Sibeth drowned Kanzua herself?
How long before the sisters' partnership breaks the moment Maghra's family reappears?

characters.name: Baba Voss
characters.line: Alkenny leader and adoptive father of the twins; a former Trivantian slaver now closing on his brother Edo's city to save Haniwa.

characters.name: Maghra
characters.line: Baba's wife, secretly Princess of House Kane; now ruling beside her sister, cut off from the family she thinks is still on the run.

characters.name: Sibeth Kane (Queen Kane)
characters.line: The Payan Queen who drowned Kanzua to hold her crown; joint monarch with Maghra and quietly the more dangerous of the two.

characters.name: Haniwa
characters.line: Sighted twin, headstrong; a prisoner inside Trivantes at the personal order of General Edo Voss.

characters.name: Kofun
characters.line: Sighted twin, more cautious than his sister; on foot with Baba and Paris, heading to Trivantes to free her.

characters.name: Paris
characters.line: Alkenny seer and keeper of Jerlamarel's letters; the one who told the twins the truth, travelling now with Baba and Kofun.

characters.name: Tamacti Jun
characters.line: The sisters' Witchfinder General; struck down at the City of Worms by Kane and Boots and believed dead.

characters.name: Edo Voss
characters.line: Baba's estranged Trivantian brother, a rising general who has just taken Haniwa and knows exactly who her father is.

characters.name: Jerlamarel
characters.line: The twins' sighted birth father; blinded by Baba after trading Haniwa to Edo, no longer a refuge or a leader.

beats.label: S2 · Rescue in Trivantes
beats.text: Baba infiltrates Trivantes to save Haniwa from his own brother Edo. Aided by sighted Lieutenant Wren, they escape with Tamacti Jun — thought dead — in tow.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reunites the family and puts Tamacti Jun back on the board, the man who can expose Sibeth.

beats.label: S2 · A political marriage
beats.text: Queen Kane names Pennsa her new capital and forces Maghra into a marriage with Lord Harlan, sealing her hold on the city as she readies war with Trivantes.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Installs Harlan as a permanent third party in Maghra's marriage and the palace politics of S3.

beats.label: S2 · The Queen's heir
beats.text: Kane declares sight is no longer witchcraft and demands a prophesied sighted heir. Drugged with Thornflower, Kofun beds her in secret; her pregnancy soon follows.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Creates the child that becomes both Sibeth's shield and the crisis at the centre of S3.

beats.label: S2 · Summit and Wren
beats.text: Kane sabotages Harlan's peace talks with a Payan ambush. Wren survives, sleeps with Haniwa, then rides back to Edo convinced Haniwa betrayed her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the Wren–Haniwa rift and forecloses any diplomatic exit from the war.

beats.label: S2 · Kane deposed
beats.text: Tamacti Jun exposes Kane before the court and calls for her head. Only Paris's revelation of the pregnancy spares her; the deposed queen is placed under house arrest.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains why Sibeth is alive but caged when S3 opens — and why the baby is the only reason.

beats.label: S2 · Greenhill Gap
beats.text: At Greenhill Gap the Payans crush Trivantes; Baba kills Edo. Maghra is crowned Queen, Tamacti Jun her High General, the Witchfinders reformed as her Royal Guard.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Redraws every allegiance: the family holds Paya, the Witchfinders now serve them, Edo is gone.

beats.label: S2 · Paris dies, Baba leaves, Tormada rises
beats.text: Sibeth admits Kofun fathered her child, then murders Paris when she moves against her. Baba slips out of Pennsa alone; in Trivantes, Oloman demonstrates a new weapon.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The exact three-way setup S3 opens on: Sibeth caged with the baby, Baba absent, Tormada armed.

cliffhanger.text: Maghra rules Paya but her sister is caged under her own roof, pregnant with Kofun's child and untouchable because of it. Baba has walked out into the mountains, and a Trivantian named Oloman has just shown his masters a weapon that no army in this world has ever faced.
questions: What does Maghra do with a sister whose baby is now her family's blood?
Will Kofun claim a child fathered on his aunt under drugs?
Can Payan swords stop a weapon Payans have never even heard?

characters.name: Maghra
characters.line: Crowned Queen of Paya after deposing her sister; planning to raise Sibeth's unborn child as her own.

characters.name: Baba Voss
characters.line: Killed his brother Edo, reunited his family, then slipped out of Pennsa alone; unreachable in the mountains.

characters.name: Sibeth Kane
characters.line: Deposed and under house arrest, pregnant with Kofun's child, and now the murderer of Paris.

characters.name: Haniwa
characters.line: Living openly sighted in Pennsa, still raw from Wren's return to Trivantes as an enemy.

characters.name: Kofun
characters.line: Unknowing father of Sibeth's child; training under Toad and unmoored by what the Queen did to him.

characters.name: Tamacti Jun
characters.line: Revealed alive; exposed Sibeth in open court and is now High General of Maghra's Paya.

characters.name: Lord Harlan
characters.line: Maghra's political husband and lord of Pennsa; sharper than he looks, and grieving his dead brother Kerrigan.

characters.name: Wren
characters.line: Sighted Trivantian officer and Haniwa's lover; back with her people, convinced Haniwa lured her into an ambush.

characters.name: Edo Voss
characters.line: Baba's brother and Trivantes' warhawk general; killed by Baba at Greenhill Gap, leaving a power vacuum at home.

characters.name: Tormada
characters.line: Trivantian Commander to whom Oloman has just unveiled an explosive weapon powerful enough to reshape a war.

beats.label: S3 · A blind heir
beats.text: Sibeth births her promised sighted heir — but Wolffe is blind. The prophecy that spared her collapses, and Kofun is left holding a son he cannot yet claim.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Destroys Sibeth's only real protection and reframes Kofun as a reluctant father overnight.

beats.label: S3 · Bow Lion killed
beats.text: In the mountains a Trivantian bomb tears Bow Lion apart. Baba heads back to Pennsa to warn Maghra that Trivantes has a weapon Payan swords cannot answer.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The event that pulls Baba out of self-exile and back into the war.

beats.label: S3 · The Witchfinders turn
beats.text: Rogue Witchfinders reject Maghra's decree that sight is no longer heresy; Tamacti Jun kills Lucien, but Sibeth turns the movement's faith toward her from house arrest.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Gives Sibeth a base of fanatics inside Paya, which is what makes her escape dangerous.

beats.label: S3 · Tormada's bomb children
beats.text: Baba's group reach the House of Enlightenment: Tormada's bombs are built by Jerlamarel's captured sighted children, and Harlan is exposed as a Trivantian collaborator.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the mechanism behind the weapon and turns Harlan from ally into a man with a debt to pay.

beats.label: S3 · Sibeth and Tormada allied
beats.text: Sibeth escapes house arrest and rides into Tormada's camp. The deposed queen and the Trivantian scientist forge the alliance that will burn Pennsa.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Merges the two threats into one; from here everything is aimed at Pennsa.

beats.label: S3 · Pennsa in flames
beats.text: Tormada's bombs rain on Pennsa, killing thousands. Harlan dies delivering the warning that empties the tunnels; Kofun is captured trying to reach Wolffe.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The disaster the whole season has been building toward, and the moment Harlan finally earns his place.

beats.label: S3 · Two sacrifices
beats.text: Maghra kills Sibeth in her tent as Baba sacrifices himself to destroy the last of Tormada's bomb stores. Haniwa and Wren leave Pennsa to find other sighted people.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes every open thread: the weapon, the sister, and the marriage — and points the survivors in three different directions.

cliffhanger.text: Pennsa stands again on new terms. Maghra rules a kingdom that has just been rewritten by a weapon, Kofun is raising a blind son fathered on his aunt, and Haniwa has ridden out with Wren to find people like herself.
questions: Will Kofun take the throne Maghra is holding open for him?
Can peace with Trivantes survive without Baba, Harlan or Sibeth to shape it?
What waits for Haniwa and Wren in a world of sighted people beyond Payan borders?

characters.name: Maghra
characters.line: Queen of a rebuilt Pennsa; killed her own sister to end the war and now rules widowed.

characters.name: Kofun
characters.line: Father of Wolffe and, by Maghra's design, next in line for the Payan throne.

characters.name: Haniwa
characters.line: Riding out of Pennsa with Wren to seek out other sighted people beyond the kingdoms.

characters.name: Wren
characters.line: Freed from Trivantian service and reunited with Haniwa; leaving Paya with her for a new life.

characters.name: Wolffe
characters.line: The blind infant son of Kofun and Sibeth, now Kofun's to raise.

characters.name: Tamacti Jun
characters.line: Maghra's High General, having crushed the Witchfinder insurgency and stayed her enforcer in the rebuild.

characters.name: Baba Voss
characters.line: Dead; sacrificed himself destroying the last of Tormada's bomb stores.

characters.name: Sibeth Kane
characters.line: Dead; killed by Maghra in her camp during the assault on Pennsa.

characters.name: Lord Harlan
characters.line: Dead; sacrificed himself at a cannibal camp to get the warning through in time to empty the tunnels.

characters.name: Tormada
characters.line: The Trivantian bombmaker whose weapons burned Pennsa; his stores destroyed with Baba in the final assault.
